title: Tabular Population Priors as Structured Retrieval for EHR Medication Set Prediction
abstract: arXiv:2611.17341v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Medication prediction from electronic health records is a fixed vocabulary structured prediction problem, yet recent clinical RAG systems often treat it like open ended case based reasoning: retrieve similar patient admissions and ask an LLM to infer a medication set. This retrieval object is indirect the model receives retrieved patient records while the target is a discrete set of medication class labels. We propose a more task aligned retrieval object: a tabular population prior ranked medication class candidates from a sparse condition medication co occurrence table estimated from training admissions. Using PACERAG as a fixed downstream pipeline and replacing only its patient retriever, this drop in swap improves F1 from 0.303 to 0.338 (+11.5% relative) and Jaccard from 0.218 to 0.237 on 1,004 heldout MIMIC IV admissions, with no additional LLM calls and no inference time patient index. A non LLM top k baseline reaches F1=0.248, conf

translated_title: 表格化人群先验作为电子健康记录药物集合预测的结构化检索
translated_abstract: 从电子健康记录（EHR）中预测药物是一个固定词表的结构化预测问题，然而近期的临床RAG系统常常将其当作开放式的基于案例的推理来处理：检索相似的患者入院记录，再让大语言模型（LLM）推断药物集合。这种检索对象是间接的——模型接收的是检索到的患者记录，而预测目标却是一个离散的药物类别标签集合。我们提出了一个与任务更加对齐的检索对象：表格化的人群先验——基于从训练入院记录中估计的稀疏“条件-药物”共现表生成、按排名排序的药物类别候选列表。以PACERAG作为固定的下游流水线，仅替换其中的患者检索器，这一即插即用的替换在1,004条MIMIC-IV留出入院记录上将F1从0.303提升至0.338（相对提升11.5%），将Jaccard从0.218提升至0.237，且无需额外的LLM调用，也无需推理时的患者索引。一个非LLM的top-k基线达到F1=0.248，进一步表……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 该论文提出用从训练数据估计的条件-药物共现表构建的表格化人群先验，替代临床RAG系统中的患者记录检索，作为更贴合药物集合预测任务的结构化检索对象，在MIMIC-IV数据上无需额外LLM调用和推理时患者索引即可显著提升F1和Jaccard指标。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes a tabular population prior—ranked medication class candidates from a sparse condition-medication co-occurrence table—as a task-aligned structured retrieval object to replace patient retrievers in clinical RAG systems, significantly improving F1 and Jaccard on MIMIC-IV medication set prediction without extra LLM calls or inference-time patient indexing.
